data.narrative:
Wiliot is a Series C semiconductor/chips company founded by Tal Tamir, Yaron Elboim, and Alon Yehezkely that has raised $364M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in the same sector and stage band, including Tenstorrent, Nearfield Instruments, Positron AI, and DEEPX.

Two valuation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier to total capital raised ($364M), yielding $619M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Tenstorrent at $2.7B, Nearfield at $1.6B, Positron AI at $1.0B, and DEEPX at $529M) produces a median of $1.3B, with a range of $529M to $2.7B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because Wiliot's revenue is not on file, limiting use of the 18.9x sector P/S median across public semiconductors.

Triangulating the two applicable methods yields a valuation range of $526M (low) to $1.5B (high), with a median of $959M. The wide spread reflects stage and business-model heterogeneity within the peer set. Key uncertainties include revenue scale and growth trajectory, which would narrow the public-comp band, and the degree to which Wiliot's technology and market traction align with higher-valued Series D peers versus lower-valued Series C contemporaries.
